Apps from other sources are not checked by Komora. An app can steal your data, spy on you, show ads or harm the phone, and an author can hand a repository over to someone else. Komora only makes sure that updates come with the same key as the first install: it cannot tell whether an app is honest.\n\nInstall only apps whose authors you know and trust.
You install these apps at your own risk. Komora and its author are not responsible for them or for any harm they may cause.

A word from the author, how to support Ukraine, licence and code

Komora was made to be a collection of apps of my own, with no ads, no tracking and no accounts. The idea came while I was working at my laptop in near darkness: after yet another Russian drone attack, the power was gone again. Every app here is free software: its code is open, and anyone can check what it does. Freedom in software is not a small thing. It is the right to know what happens on your phone, and not to hand your life to anyone.
Komora was made in Ukraine. The names of its apps and themes carry words from home. This is who we are, and it is alive. We are alive.

Yet since 2014, and since 24 February 2022 at full force, Russia has been waging war against my country. Every day, missiles and drones strike cities, homes, hospitals and power plants. The occupiers kill, abduct Ukrainian children, destroy museums, churches and libraries, and ban our language in the lands they hold. Their aim is for Ukrainians to cease to exist as a people.
We are fighting for the right to be: to live on our own land, speak our own language, create our own things. The freedom you value in software is, for us today, a matter of life.
If Komora is useful to you, please support Ukraine. I receive none of this money: the links go straight to the organisations\' official sites.
If you are from Ukraine: thank you for being here. We hold on. We defend, we donate, we look after one another and we choose Ukrainian: together, this brings victory closer.
The links open in your browser, on the organisations\' own sites. Komora knows nothing about it and receives nothing.
